description:
No spec subject — bookkeeping epic.

Impromptu epic created 2026-07-26 to land four independently-surfaced follow-up tickets on a SINGLE PR. Children were each carved by an earlier ticket's cold verification or critical review and had no owning epic (gai was reparented here from specled_-xkn; xkn retains its other three children).

Children and the subjects they advance:
  - specled_-48i  specled.package      content-lint verification for adoption_guide/concepts_guide must requirements
  - specled_-vk0  specled.package      doc-identifier lint hardening (lookbehind bounds, severity-corpus asymmetry, digit codes, stale-marker sweep, two-way mirror)
  - specled_-gai  specled.spec_review  retire duplicated coverage_tab_bind_closure compound statement, repoint lib/** covers markers
  - specled_-ymn  specled.verification cross_vm_temp_names ADR vs hash_store fixed-name .tmp sibling; tracer pid-separation falsifiability; ADR affects: reach

Sequencing rationale: 48i and vk0 both edit .spec/specs/package.spec.md (48i the adoption_guide/concepts_guide verification entries, vk0 the decisions: list plus must wording), so 48i blocks vk0 to avoid a real same-file merge conflict. gai and ymn touch disjoint specs and lib files and run concurrently with 48i.

Orchestrated by /orchestrate-epic. Implementers: Codex. Verify/audit/rebase: Claude.

Generated/derived state policy for this epic:
  - .spec/state.json — derived, untracked, gitignored; never review scope, never committed. Regenerate with `mix spec.index --output .spec/state.json`.
  - .spec/realization_hashes.json — COMMITTED baseline, NOT free generated state. Per .claude/rules/specled.md a rebase worker must NOT resolve conflicts here by regenerating (that silently absorbs realization drift). On conflict prefer the side whose branch legitimately changed the named bindings, or keep both entries when different bindings moved.

Merge gate for this repo (host mix, no compose):
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check
Hash inputs for the unchanged-tree skip: lib, test, config, priv, mix.lock, .spec.

specled_-vk0 held: blocked by specled_-48i (shared .spec/specs/package.spec.md). Spawns in wave 2 off the post-48i epic HEAD.

All four ticket descriptions were rewritten during admission into canonical scope contracts (## Pre-flight corrections / ## Allowed touches / ## Out of Scope (files) / ## Out of Scope (intent) / ## Verification (gates)); the earlier ORCHESTRATOR ADMISSION comments are marked SUPERSEDED. Admission found and corrected four substantive ticket defects: gai's marker inventory undercounted 4 lib files/6 markers as 3 files; 48i's gap was already largely closed by cz0/0x4 and is now scoped to concepts_guide only; ymn advances specled.verification but edits a specled.binding-owned file (co-change authorized explicitly); vk0's family-widening item was already shipped by cz0.

Side finding filed standalone as specled_-pii (not adopted into this epic — not required for any child to succeed): the subject-lookup command documented in .claude/rules/beadwork.md and specled.md, bw list --grep "Advances:.*<subject.id>", silently returns zero because --grep is a literal substring search.

LESSONS
- [untested-clause] Assert a doc clause with needles UNIQUE to its section, or scope the search to the text between its heading and the next heading; bare identifier tokens are satisfied incidentally by unrelated prose elsewhere in the same file, leaving the clause guarded by its heading alone (from specled_-48i)

- [other] Before adding an assertion, grep the existing spec-verification block for the same clause. A new assertion that duplicates an existing byte-exact check — especially a weaker substring of it — is scope creep and bounces, even when the surrounding work is correct (from specled_-48i)
- [untested-clause] Run the falsifiability gate against the SPECIFIC clause you strengthened, not whichever clause is convenient. Demonstrating a break on an already-load-bearing assertion proves nothing about the weak one (from specled_-48i)

It only fires the reverse direction (`verification_target_missing_reference`) and only when no valid marker remains; `scenario_unknown_cover` is a different code path for bad ids inside SPEC verification entries. Validate lib/test markers by grep against the real id corpus (from specled_-gai; corrects a false premise the orchestrator had written into that ticket's gate)
- [stale-spec] Deleting or shrinking a requirement statement without restating every normative `shall` clause it carried is spec weakening by omission, and `spec.check` CANNOT see it because it is prose. Before shrinking a requirement, diff the old statement against the union of surviving statements, account for every dropped clause, and check whether any `.spec/decisions/` consequence line still depends on the sentence being removed (from specled_-gai)
- [other] When repointing a marker, if NO existing requirement states the contract that call site implements, do not park it on a statement-free umbrella — that manufactures an unfalsifiable `must`. Either write the requirement or surface the gap (from specled_-gai)

- [stale-spec] A SUPERSEDING ADR must carry forward every normative clause of the ADR it replaces — prohibitions AND carve-outs. Dropping a carve-out silently narrows policy, and dropping a prohibition silently widens it; neither is visible to `spec.check`. Diff the old Decision section against the new one clause by clause (from specled_-ymn, which dropped the very test-only carve-out its own Out of Scope relied on)
- [other] Extend an ADR's `affects:` only for subjects whose DOMAIN the decision governs — never because a shared surface file (e.g. verifier.ex) happens to appear on that subject's `surface:` list. Surface coincidence makes the spec graph assert something false, which is the mirror image of under-claiming reach. Prove necessity by removing the entry and re-running the gate (from specled_-ymn)
- [other] Collapsing duplicated narration to a one-line pointer is only safe if the pointer TARGET actually contains the specifics being removed. Verify the target AFTER the edit; a commit that trims sites and genericises the target at the same time destroys the rationale it claims to centralise (from specled_-ymn)
